user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Prerequisites (Night Before)

- [ ] Install `git-svn` (`git svn` command available)
- [ ] Identify SVN repo URL and confirm access
- [ ] Confirm team size and notify stakeholders of freeze window
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository

---

## Timeline Overview

| Time | Phase |
|------|-------|
| 08:00–09:00 | Prep & author mapping |
| 09:00–11:00 | Clone & convert |
| 11:00–12:00 | Clean up & verify |
| 12:00–13:00 | Lunch buffer / contingency |
| 13:00–14:00 | Push to remote Git host |
| 14:00–15:00 | Team onboarding |
| 15:00–16:00 | Smoke testing |
| 16:00–17:00 | Final checks & SVN lock |

---

## Phase 1 — Prep & Author Mapping (08:00–09:00)

### 1.1 Freeze SVN commits
```bash
# Notify team: no SVN commits after 08:00
# Or set repo to read-only via svnadmin
svnadmin setlog /path/to/repo -r HEAD --bypass-hooks "FROZEN: migrating to Git"
```

### 1.2 Create author mapping file
```bash
# Get all SVN authors
svn log svn://your-repo-url --quiet | \
  grep "^r" | awk '{print $3}' | sort -u > authors.txt

# Build authors-transform.txt manually:
# format: svn_username = Full Name <email@example.com>
```

**`authors-transform.txt` example:**
```
jsmith = John Smith <jsmith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mjones@company.com>
```

---

## Phase 2 — Clone & Convert (09:00–11:00)

### 2.1 Clone SVN repo using git-svn

**Standard layout (trunk/branches/tags):**
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors-transform.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -A authors-transform.txt \
  my-project-git
```

**Non-standard layout:**
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --trunk=trunk \
  --branches=branches \
  --tags=tags \
  --authors-file=authors-transform.txt \
  my-project-git
```

> ⏱️ For small repos this typically takes **5–30 minutes**

### 2.2 Verify the clone
```bash
cd my-project-git
git log --oneline -20        # Check commit history
git branch -a                # Check branches
```

---

## Phase 3 — Clean Up & Verify (11:00–12:00)

### 3.1 Convert SVN tags to proper Git tags
```bash
# List remote SVN tags
git branch -r | grep tags/

# Convert each to a real Git tag
for tag in $(git branch -r | grep 'tags/' | sed 's/.*tags\///'); do
  git tag "$tag" "refs/remotes/tags/$tag"
  git branch -r -d "tags/$tag"
done
```

### 3.2 Convert remote branches to local branches
```bash
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v 'tags/' | grep -v 'trunk'); do
  name=$(echo "$branch" | sed 's/.*\///')
  git branch "$name" "$branch"
done
```

### 3.3 Clean up git-svn references
```bash
git for-each-ref refs/remotes | cut -d/ -f3- | \
  while read ref; do git branch -rd "origin/$ref" 2>/dev/null; done

# Remove git-svn config sections
git config --remove-section svn-remote.svn 2>/dev/null
rm -rf .git/svn
```

### 3.4 Verify history integrity
```bash
git log --oneline --graph --all   # Visual branch check
git diff HEAD~5 HEAD              # Sanity check recent changes
wc -l <(svn log svn://your-repo-url) # Compare commit counts roughly
```

---

## Phase 4 — Push to Remote Git Host (13:00–14:00)

### 4.1 Create remote repo
- Create empty repo on **GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket** (no README, no .gitignore)

### 4.2 Add remote and push everything
```bash
cd my-project-git

git remote add origin git@github.com:org/my-project.git

# Push all branches
git push origin --all

# Push all tags
git push origin --tags
```

### 4.3 Set default branch
```bash
git push origin main   # or master, depending on your trunk name
# Set as default in GitHub/GitLab UI
```

---

## Phase 5 — Team Onboarding (14:00–15:00)

### Each developer runs:
```bash
# Remove old SVN working copy, then:
git clone git@github.com:org/my-project.git
cd my-project
git checkout main
```

### Share a quick-reference cheat sheet:

| SVN Command | Git Equivalent |
|-------------|----------------|
| `svn update` | `git pull` |
| `svn commit` | `git add . && git commit && git push` |
| `svn status` | `git status` |
| `svn log` | `git log` |
| `svn diff` | `git diff` |
| `svn revert` | `git checkout -- <file>` |
| `svn branch` | `git checkout -b <branch>` |

---

## Phase 6 — Smoke Testing (15:00–16:00)

- [ ] Each developer clones and opens the project successfully
- [ ] Build/CI pipeline runs against new Git repo
- [ ] Update any CI/CD config (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, etc.) to point to Git
- [ ] Verify `.gitignore` covers what `.svnignore` did
- [ ] Check that no large/binary files were accidentally included

### Convert SVN ignore to Git ignore:
```bash
cd my-project-git
git svn show-ignore > .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "Add .gitignore from SVN ignore properties"
git push
```

---

## Phase 7 — Final Checks & SVN Lock (16:00–17:00)

- [ ] Archive SVN repo (do **not** delete it yet — keep for 30 days)
- [ ] Make SVN repo permanently read-only
- [ ] Update internal wiki/docs with new Git repo URL
- [ ] Update issue tracker links if needed
- [ ] Send team confirmation email

```bash
# Make SVN read-only via pre-commit hook
echo '#!/bin/sh
echo "This repository has been migrated to Git."
echo "New repo: git@github.com:org/my-project.git"
exit 1' > /path/to/svn/repo/hooks/pre-commit
chmod +x /path/to/svn/repo/hooks/pre-commit
```

---

## Rollback Plan

If something goes wrong before 13:00:
1. SVN repo is still intact and writable — just unfreeze it
2. Discard the local git clone and start over

If something goes wrong after 13:00:
1. Re-enable SVN pre-commit hook removal
2. Communicate delay to team
3. Retry next morning with lessons learned

---

## Common Pitfalls

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Unknown SVN author | Add missing entry to `authors-transform.txt` and re-run |
| Large binary files bloating repo | Use `git-filter-repo` to remove them post-migration |
| Merge history not preserved | SVN mergeinfo doesn't map cleanly to Git — document known gaps |
| Branches missing | Check non-standard SVN layout and adjust `--branches` path |
| CI/CD broken | Update webhook URLs and credentials in pipeline config |

---

> ✅ **End of day goal:** Team is committing to Git, SVN is read-only, history is intact.

Based on the migration plan above, the top 3 risks are:

---

## Top 3 Risks

### 1. 🔴 Incomplete/Corrupt History Transfer
**What can go wrong:**
- Unknown SVN authors break the clone mid-process
- Non-standard repo layout causes branches or tags to be missed
- Commit count mismatch between SVN and Git

**Impact:** High — lost history is very hard to recover after SVN is locked

**Mitigation:**
- Build the author map carefully the night before
- Verify commit counts and branch list before pushing to remote
- Keep SVN read-only (not deleted) for 30 days as a fallback

---

### 2. 🟠 CI/CD Pipeline Breaks
**What can go wrong:**
- Build system still points to SVN repo URL
- Authentication credentials don't carry over
- Webhook triggers, environment variables, or scripts reference SVN paths

**Impact:** Medium-High — blocks the whole team from shipping code

**Mitigation:**
- Audit all pipeline configs before migration day
- Test a build against the new Git repo before declaring success
- Have a pipeline owner available during the afternoon phases

---

### 3. 🟡 Team Adoption Friction
**What can go wrong:**
- Developers unfamiliar with Git accidentally push to wrong branches
- SVN mental model (e.g. expecting linear history) causes confusion
- Someone commits to the old SVN repo after the freeze

**Impact:** Medium — causes rework and potential data inconsistency

**Mitigation:**
- Enforce the SVN freeze with a hard pre-commit hook, not just an email
- Distribute the SVN→Git cheat sheet before migration day
- Designate one person as the Git help desk for the first week

---

> 💡 **Biggest single risk overall:** History corruption (#1) — because it's the hardest to detect quickly and the hardest to fix after the fact.

## Migration Day Checklist

### Before You Start
- [ ] SVN repo backed up
- [ ] Author mapping file complete
- [ ] Team notified of commit freeze

### During Migration
- [ ] SVN commits frozen
- [ ] `git svn clone` completed successfully
- [ ] Commit count verified against SVN
- [ ] Branches and tags confirmed present
- [ ] `.gitignore` created from SVN ignore
- [ ] Pushed to remote Git host

### Before Closing Out
- [ ] CI/CD pipeline updated and tested
- [ ] Every developer has cloned the new repo
- [ ] SVN made permanently read-only
- [ ] New repo URL communicated to team

> ✅ All boxes checked = safe to call the migration done.

## Rollback Option

**Re-enable the SVN repository.**

If anything goes wrong, remove the pre-commit hook that blocks writes, notify the team to resume using SVN, and discard the Git clone.

```bash
rm /path/to/svn/repo/hooks/pre-commit
```

> ⚠️ This only works if SVN was kept read-only rather than deleted — which is why you should **never delete the SVN repo on migration day.**

## One Prerequisite

**`git-svn` must be installed** on the machine running the migration.

```bash
# Verify it's available
git svn --version
```

> Without this, the `git svn clone` command will fail and the migration cannot start.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
## Fastest Validation Step

**Compare commit counts between SVN and Git.**

```bash
# SVN commit count
svn log svn://your-repo-url --quiet | grep -c "^r"

# Git commit count
git rev-list HEAD --count
```

> If the numbers match, history transferred correctly. Takes less than **30 seconds** and catches the most critical migration error immediately.

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
## Two Tools

### 1. `git-svn`
Converts the SVN repository into a Git repository, preserving commit history and authors.

### 2. `git-filter-repo`
Cleans up the migrated repo — removes unwanted large files or binary blobs before pushing to the remote host.

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text:
## Final Cutover Approval

**The project or team lead** should approve the final cutover — they are accountable for confirming that:

- History looks correct
- The team is ready to switch
- CI/CD is working against the new repo

> No one should lock SVN or announce completion without their explicit sign-off.

## Communication Tip

**Send one clear message before and one after** — tell the team exactly when SVN is freezing and then confirm when Git is live, including the new repo URL.

> Avoid a flood of updates during the migration itself — it creates confusion and interrupts focus.

## Final Recap

A 1-day SVN to Git migration for a small repo is straightforward if kept disciplined.

| What | Key Point |
|------|-----------|
| **Tool** | `git-svn` does the heavy lifting |
| **Biggest risk** | Incomplete history transfer |
| **Fastest check** | Compare commit counts |
| **Rollback** | Keep SVN read-only, never delete it |
| **Approval** | Team lead signs off before cutover |
| **Communication** | One message before, one message after |
| **Done when** | SVN is locked, team is on Git, CI/CD is green |

> ✅ Prepare the night before, execute cleanly during the day, verify before you lock — and the migration should be finished by 17:00.

- Prep the night before
- Freeze SVN at start of day
- Use `git-svn` to clone
- Verify commit counts immediately
- Push to remote Git host
- Update CI/CD pipeline
- Team lead approves cutover
- Lock SVN, never delete it
- Send one final message to team
- Done by 17:00
